title: Augustus
summary: Augustus, born Gaius Octavius, was the first emperor of Rome, establishing the Principate after decades of civil strife following the assassination of his adoptive father Julius Caesar. Consolidating supreme executive, military, and religious authority while maintaining Republican facades, Augustus initiated the Pax Romana—two centuries of imperial peace and stability. His institutional reorganization, extensive building programs, and fiscal reforms laid the enduring governing architecture of the Roman Empire until its collapse.

uncertainty.note: Birth on 23 September 63 BCE and death on 19 August 14 CE at Nola are both securely documented by contemporary records and Suetonius.

where.modern_name: Rome, Lazio, Italy (principal seat of power; born in Rome, died at Nola in Campania)
where.historical_name: Roma, capital of the Roman Empire

importance.justification: Founder of the Roman Principate and creator of the administrative system that sustained the empire for centuries.
